sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of predicted default, and risk rises as utilization goes up.
The jump is sharpest at about 72% utilization, where the added risk becomes large compared with lower levels.
Past delinquencies are the second or third most important driver, and having any delinquency raises risk.
Income is also a second or third most important driver, and higher income is associated with lower risk.
Length of credit history matters at most weakly, with longer histories associated with somewhat lower risk.
The data do not settle how much the debt-to-income ratio matters, since its estimated effect is small and uncertain.
The effect of utilization on default risk is at least as large when there are past delinquencies, though the data leave this interaction only partly settled.
The data do not settle whether the effect of utilization grows with length of credit history.
Age hardly matters for the model's predictions.
